title: Election night surprise on financial sector stocks

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We will employ an event study methodology to assess the impact of the unexpected election outcome on financial sector stocks. The key assumption is that the market model, estimated using the pre-event period [−10,−2], accurately captures the expected returns of the stocks. The event window [0,+3] will be used to calculate the abnormal returns. The main assumption here is that the election outcome is an unexpected event that does not directly affect the market model's parameters.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s15_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns using the market model
data <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  mutate(ar = ret - (beta * mkt_ret))

# Calculate cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) for the event window
event_window_car <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= 0 & event_day <= 3) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car = sum(ar))

# Calculate the average CAR across all stocks
avg_car <- mean(event_window_car$car)

# Print the average CAR
print(paste("Average CAR: ", avg_car))

# Perform a basic robustness check: t-test for the average CAR
t_stat <- mean(event_window_car$car) / (sd(event_window_car$car) / sqrt(length(event_window_car$car)))
print(paste("T-statistic: ", t_stat))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the average cumulative abnormal return (CAR) for the financial sector stocks to be positive, indicating that the unexpected election outcome generated abnormal returns for these stocks in the [0,+3] post-election window. The magnitude of the CAR will depend on the actual impact of the election outcome on the financial sector. A CAR of around 5-10% would be a reasonable estimate, considering the potential impact of an unexpected election outcome on the financial markets. However, the actual magnitude may vary depending on the specific circumstances of the election and the financial sector's exposure to the election outcome.
